result.title: Same Pixels, Different Documents: Measuring Part-Level Editability in Image Vectorization
result.summary: Image vectorization is often evaluated by rendering fidelity, which cannot distinguish documents that render identically but support different edits. Edit-based evaluation tests outcomes, but an oracle that gathers a part's fragments can conceal the cost of selecting them. We introduce Pass@k, which tests whether a prescribed edit can succeed using objects selectable within k clicks under a specified interaction model. Eight document diagnostics characterize properties relevant to editing beyond these tasks. We assess structural sensitivity through controlled perturbations, practical relevance through designer operations, and reference dependence through alternative drawings. We evaluate twelve open and commercial methods on 211 references, with 635 edit tasks on 93 of them. In each of four reference sets, including two drawn by designers, 64-88% of oracle-passed tasks on parts composed of multiple shapes fail at Pass@1, against 6-40% for single shapes, pooling counts over configurations. Higher fidelity does not guarantee higher Pass@1, while selected diagnostics are associated with designers' effort in our study.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对图像矢量化提出以可编辑性而非渲染保真度评估文档质量，设计 Pass@k 指标：在指定交互模型下，预设编辑能否用 k 次点击内可选中的对象完成，并在 211 个参考图像、635 个编辑任务上对比十二种商用与开源方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心论点「保真度相同或更高的表示未必支持相同的干预」以及按操作成本而非重建误差设计的评价方式，可能为 LVR 中「latent 状态是否真正可用、可被定向干预」的评价思路提供类比线索，需核查其任务与指标定义是否可迁移。
